checks: A bounded convex nonempty r-dimensional fiber contains an r-simplex and has finite positive intrinsic r-volume. Compactness makes the collection finite. Fibers below q carry zero q-mass. At q=0, convexity puts the combination in the singleton target and counting gives a=1, including the d=0 case.

With all coefficients positive, holding the other summands fixed supplies each input direction to the direction of the sum. Every difference in the sum belongs to the sum of the input directions. Target dimension at most q and each input dimension q therefore force a common q-direction, including for the target, before Brunn–Minkowski is used.

Brunn–Minkowski in the common q-space gives at least a, while inclusion and maximality give at most a. Strict separation of an outside point and mixing it with an interior ball proves a proper compact convex inclusion in that common affine plane would increase volume. Thus the target equals the Minkowski average.

Two positive equal volumes force equality homotheties to be translations. For more inputs, every grouped inequality is an equality and the average of the other summands has volume a, so induction gives common translates. Translating and averaging then makes the centroid affine for precisely these combinations.

A convex representation of an integer section of the centroid hull has finitely many positive terms after discarding zero weights. The incidence identity gives a unique centroid there, and the reverse inclusion follows from the generators. Projecting gives lattice completeness.
